name: multiple_choice: A sociologist uses data from the General Social Survey…

request.questionText: A sociologist uses data from the General Social Survey to estimate the typical "occupational prestige factor" of professions of U.S. adult residents. The survey includes a variable called Prestige, a numerical scale 0-100 for job prestige attempting to measure the level of respect/admiration for the job in society. In the sample, survey respondents' have a median prestige score of 45.1. The sociologist uses bootstrapping to calculate a 95% confidence interval for the population median prestige score: (44, 46) Which of the following is an accurate interpretation of this analysis? Choose the best answer.

choices.label: A
choices.text: We are 95% confident that between 44% -- 46% of U.S. adults have a prestige score association with their occupation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: We are 95% confident that the true median prestige score for U.S. adults is 45.1.

choices.label: C
choices.text: We are confident that 95% of all U.S. adults have an occupation with a prestige score between 44 and 46.

choices.label: D
choices.text: We are 95% confident that the interval 44-46 contains the true median prestige score for U.S. adults.
